title: God, isn’t he dreadful?
html_source:
Confirming the character of Mulligan’s Catholicism, his casual blasphemy–twice in one speech–tells us that he is as insincere as he is outwardly conformist. A sharp contrast to Stephen.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: To clarify, I’m not suggesting this means ‘Isn’t God dreadful’, I’m suggesting that Buck’s casual use of ‘God’ as an exclamation of frustration is blasphemous. These things help us to see how superficial Mulligan’s Catholicism is: he literally goes through the motions, while failing to follow the spirit of the religion. Just the opposite of Stephen’s awkward refusal to say things he doesn’t wholeheartedly believe in.
